mission.title: Install and Configure Rancher / RKE2
mission.description: Rancher is a complete container management platform that simplifies the deployment and management of Kubernetes clusters across various environments. It is ideal for organizations looking to manage multiple Kubernetes clusters with ease, but it requires careful resource management and monitoring to ensure optimal performance.

steps.title: Install the Rancher CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Rancher CLI, which is necessary for managing Rancher from the command line.

```bash

curl -L https://github.com/rancher/cli/releases/download/v2.14.3/rancher-darwin-amd64 -o rancher && chmod +x rancher && sudo mv rancher /usr/local/bin/

```

> For macOS users; adjust the URL for Linux or Windows.
commands: curl -L https://github.com/rancher/cli/releases/download/v2.14.3/rancher-darwin-amd64 -o rancher && chmod +x rancher && sudo mv rancher /usr/local/bin/

steps.title: Create a Kubernetes Cluster
steps.description:
This command creates a new Kubernetes cluster using RKE2 with specified version, node count, and region.

```bash

curl -sfL https://get.rke2.io | INSTALL_RKE2_VERSION=v1.30.0 sh -

sudo systemctl enable rke2-server && sudo systemctl start rke2-server

```

> This installs RKE2 on the server.
> This starts the RKE2 server.
commands: sudo systemctl enable rke2-server && sudo systemctl start rke2-server

steps.title: Set up kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures the kubeconfig file to allow kubectl to communicate with the newly created cluster.

```bash

sudo cat /etc/rancher/rke2/rke2.yaml > ~/.kube/config

```

> This copies the RKE2 kubeconfig to your home directory.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in the Kubernetes cluster to ensure they are ready.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see your nodes listed with a status of 'Ready'.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step involves setting up monitoring and autoscaling for your cluster.

```bash

kubectl apply -f https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/release/v2.14.3/manifests/rancher-monitoring.yaml

kubectl apply -f https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/release/v2.14.3/manifests/rancher-autoscaler.yaml

```

> This installs Rancher monitoring.
> This installs Rancher autoscaler.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Rancher
uninstall.description:
This step removes Rancher and its associated resources. Be aware that this may lead to data loss and orphaned resources.

```bash

kubectl delete -f https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/release/v2.14.3/manifests/rancher.yaml

sudo systemctl stop rke2-server && sudo systemctl disable rke2-server

```

> This deletes the Rancher deployment.
> This stops and disables the RKE2 server.
commands: sudo systemctl stop rke2-server && sudo systemctl disable rke2-server

upgrade.title: Upgrade Rancher
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your data, then upgrade Rancher and verify the installation.

```bash

kubectl get all --all-namespaces > backup.txt

kubectl apply -f https://github.com/rancher/rancher/blob/release/v2.14.3/manifests/rancher.yaml

kubectl get pods -n cattle-system

```

> Backup current resources.
> This applies the new Rancher manifest.
> Verify that all Rancher pods are running.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the kubeconfig is not set up correctly or the server certificate is not trusted.

**Fix:**
Ensure the kubeconfig file is correctly copied and permissions are set. Use 'sudo cp /etc/rancher/rke2/rke2.yaml ~/.kube/config'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to pull image: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error response from daemon: pull access denied'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the image repository is not accessible or the image does not exist.

**Fix:**
Check the image name and ensure you have access to the repository.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'node not found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the node is not registered with the cluster.

**Fix:**
Check the node status and ensure it is properly joined to the cluster.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'context deadline exceeded'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the Kubernetes API server is not reachable.

**Fix:**
Check the network connectivity and ensure the RKE2 server is running.

versionNotes.changes: Added support for Kubernetes v1.30, improved RBAC configurations, and enhanced monitoring capabilities.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated support for Kubernetes versions below 1.27.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from v2.10, ensure to migrate your configurations to the new RBAC model.
